input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims regarding the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure is present and balanced (20.4: prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, consent required for adverse settlements), and 20.5 adds the usual IP remedies (procure, modify/replace without materially reducing functionality, or terminate with a straight-line three-year refund) in addition to, not in lieu of, defence. Customer's indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Vendor's indemnity is also not squeezed by the liability cap: indemnification obligations are "Excluded Claims" under 21.3 and so sit outside the 21.1 cap, better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. (The narrow "first Order Form" cap base in 21.1 is a limitation-of-liability issue addressed under that rule, not here.)
